CRL.note: FILLED 2026-10-01: 21 @ $288.30 — Life Sciences Tools & Services, joining WAT. Net Prc is the fill; broker_statement, actual_fill, overrides ZERO, fees $0.00, capital $97,500. || THE CHEAPEST ENTRY OF ANY NAME CURRENTLY HELD, AND IT WAS PRICE THAT MADE IT SO, NOT SIZING. $4.4300 per share = 1.5366% of the fill, $93.03 initial risk on 21 shares. THE SUPERLATIVE IS BOUNDED DELIBERATELY: it was first written as 'the cheapest entry in the live record' and that is FALSE. Measured per share as a percentage of entry across all 52 entries in closed[] and holdings[], CRL is THIRD — EQT 2026-08-26 at 1.1436% and JNJ 2026-08-27 at 1.2071% are both cheaper, and both are closed. On initial risk in DOLLARS it is sixth, behind EQT $72.06, JNJ $73.60, FANG $78.90, BIIB $91.08 and DVN $91.75. What is true and worth recording: it is the cheapest of the thirteen names now held, with WAT next at 1.9429%. The board was computed on the 2026-09-30 close of 295.01, where the same 21 shares would have carried $233.94; the price fell to 288.30 before the fill and took $140.91 of risk out of the trade without changing the stop. || STOP PROVENANCE: entry_stop is the SMA20 on the 2026-09-30 CONFIRMED CLOSE, read FROM THE FRAME with the basis bar ASSERTED — 20 bars ending 2026-09-30, that bar verified present as the last row, on two reads agreeing to 0.0000 — BUT THE TWO READS ARE NOT INDEPENDENT AND THE AGREEMENT IS AN IDENTITY, NOT A MEASUREMENT. yfinance's auto_adjust=True Close IS the Yahoo v8 chart adjclose array (yfinance/scrapers/history.py fetches the same v8 chart endpoint on query2; utils.py reads indicators.adjclose[0].adjclose into 'Adj Close' and auto_adjust renames it to Close), so both reads collapse to mean(adjclose[window]) x close[basis] / adjclose[basis] and agree bit-for-bit by construction. Element-wise the two arrays differ by exactly 0.0 across all 20 bars. WHAT THE CHECK DOES COVER: the re-basing arithmetic, row alignment, and that the basis bar is present and the window is 20 bars — the holed-frame failure this project has hit three times. WHAT IT CANNOT COVER: a wrong value from Yahoo. Injecting a 10% bad print on an in-window bar moves the stop while the check still reports 0.0000 and passes. No non-Yahoo vendor was reachable to close that gap. The figure reproduces this morning's reported value and did not move. || ATR14 — TWO READINGS, NEITHER PICKED. THIS IS THE ROW AN ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER REFUSED OUTRIGHT this morning rather than average. The engine artifact carries 10.0985 and today's recomputation gives 10.1121, higher by 0.0137; the reviewer proved the closes identical by matching RSI14 to 1e-15 and showed the gap is entirely in the High/Low of the last three bars, i.e. a revision and not a hole. The entry-time extension is 0.4387x (engine) or 0.4381x (today) and the 1.8x line 302.0473 or 302.0719 — which moves the floored limit from 302.04 to 302.07. THE VALUE THAT WILL ACTUALLY FIRE IS THE SMA20 283.8700, identical on both readings and on both fetch paths; the ATR governs only the entry-time guard, which is now historical. Recorded for a future reader: scripts/auto_trader.py sizes from the COMMITTED ARTIFACT, so the limit the automation would have placed is the engine-frame 302.04, not today's 302.07. || FLOORING ON THIS TICKET IS FRAME-DEPENDENT, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT CUTS BOTH WAYS: on the ENGINE's ATR the floored limit 302.04 is 1.7993xATR and the rounded 302.05 would have been 1.8003x, OVER the guard — a save; on TODAY's ATR floor and round both give 302.07 at 1.7998x and nothing is at stake. The same revision that moved the limit three cents moved it across a cent boundary. A $6,054.30 position = 6.21% of capital. Extension at the fill well under half an ATR — the least extended entry of the seven.

APA.note: FILLED 2026-10-09: 130 @ $46.425 — Oil & Gas Exploration & Production, a NEW GROUP for this book and its only energy name. Graded A+ on the 2026-10-08 confirmed close. Net Prc is the fill; broker_statement, actual_fill, overrides ZERO, fees $0.00, capital $97,500 || THIS ROW IS TEN SESSIONS LATE AND THAT IS THE POINT OF RECORDING IT LOUDLY. The position filled 2026-10-09 and reached the ledger on 2026-10-23. For ten sessions the book carried an unrecorded holding: no row, no framed stop, and no risk counted in any heat or R28 figure — and the exit engine cannot see it at all, because position_signals reads holdings[] and an unrecorded ENTRY is invisible to it by construction (its own exit_drift_summary.covers field says so). The prompt that was to carry this fill (CCPrompt_20261009_positions.md, 10469B, injected 14:46:22Z) was written BEFORE the fill and never mentioned it || STOP PROVENANCE: entry_stop 43.9415 = the SMA20 on the 2026-10-08 CONFIRMED CLOSE, read from the frame with the basis bar ASSERTED — 20 bars 2026-09-11..2026-10-08, that bar verified present as the last row, close_on_basis 45.47. scripts/frame_stop.py reports zero corporate actions in the window and marks its raw control INERT, so the two yfinance paths agree by identity and prove nothing on their own. THE INDEPENDENT CHECK IS NASDAQ AND IT IS EXACT: api.nasdaq.com quote/APA/historical (HTTP 200) served all 20 bars and its SMA20 is 43.9415, matching to 0.0000 on a vendor that does not share Yahoo's adjclose array || A LIVE INSTANCE OF THE AMCR TRAP WAS CAUGHT FRAMING THIS STOP, AND IT IS RECORDED BECAUSE IT WOULD HAVE UNDERSTATED THE STOP. APA went ex-$0.25 on 2026-10-22. A yfinance fetch made TODAY with auto_adjust=True back-applies that dividend to every bar before it and returns an SMA20 of 43.7202 and a basis close of 45.2410 — $0.2213 a share below the correct figure, $28.77 of risk on 130 shares. The as-of rule is what excludes it: EVERY ADJUSTMENT KNOWN AT THE TRADE DATE IS APPLIED AND NO LATER ONE IS, and on 2026-10-09 the 10-22 ex-date did not exist. 43.9415 is the as-of figure and Nasdaq confirms it; 43.7202 is the artefact || ROW 2 AT THE SIGNAL BAR, NOT AT INTRADAY VALUES. On the 2026-10-08 close: SMA20 43.9415, ATR14 1.5650 (atr_mean, the simple mean of the last 14 True Ranges, not Wilder). The exact 1.8x line is 46.7584990910. FLOORED to the cent it is 46.75, admitting 1.7946xATR; ROUNDED it is 46.76, admitting 1.8010xATR — OVER THE GUARD. THE FLOORING RULE IS THE LEDGER'S CONVENTION AND THE AUTOMATION DOES NOT IMPLEMENT IT, so 'flooring earned its keep' would be the wrong credit here. scripts/auto_trader.py:406 still places order_type='limit', limit=round(c['line'], 2) - there is no floor anywhere in that path - so the limit it would have placed for APA is 46.76, the 1.8010xATR value that is OVER the guard. What kept this ticket legal is that the fill came in at 46.425, well below either line, not that anything floored it. APA is therefore a fresh instance of the open auto_trader.py:406 defect rather than a win for the rule: the kill switch is on and that path is not wired to a workflow, which is the only reason it did not matter. The fill at 46.425 sits at 1.5869xATR, $0.3250 a share INSIDE the floored line. NO BREACH || RISK: $2.4835 per share = 5.35% of the fill, $322.85 initial risk on 130 shares, a $6,035.25 position = 6.19% of capital — inside the 5-8% band. THE OPERATOR'S 3xATR ESTIMATE OVERSTATED THE RISK, in the same direction as it did on HPE: the guess of ~$4.62 a share implies $600.60, where the frame gives $322.85, so $277.75 of risk was being quoted that the position does not carry. 3xATR here is actually $4.6950; the frame's stop distance is 1.5869xATR, not 3x, because the sma20_close stop is a mean-reversion level and not an ATR multiple
